intro: Who to call and what to do when something goes wrong in the villages. If anyone is in danger, call 999.

topics.title: There's a power cut
steps: Check your trip switch first. If only your home is off, it may be your own electrics.
Call 105 (free from any phone) to report a power cut or get updates, or check the power cut map.
Keep fridge and freezer doors shut, and unplug sensitive equipment until the power is back.
If you depend on medical equipment, ask your energy supplier about the Priority Services Register.

topics.title: You smell gas
steps: Call 0800 111 999 straight away (free, 24 hours).
Don't use light switches, flames or phones near the smell. Open doors and windows.
Turn the gas off at the meter if it's safe to do so, then go outside to wait.

topics.title: There's a water leak or no water
steps: Leaks in the road or pavement, or no water: Severn Trent, 0800 783 4444.
Leaks inside your home: turn off your stopcock and call a plumber.

topics.title: It's flooding
steps: If anyone is in danger, call 999. Never walk or drive through floodwater.
Flood warnings: Floodline 0345 988 1188, or sign up for free warnings on GOV.UK.
A flooded road or blocked drain: report it to Worcestershire County Council online or on 01905 765765.
Sandbags and what to do in a flood: Wychavon's emergency flooding advice.

topics.title: You see a crime or antisocial behaviour
steps: If it's happening now or someone is in danger, call 999.
Otherwise call 101 or report it online to West Mercia Police.
To report it anonymously, call Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

topics.title: You've lost or found a pet
steps: Dogs: call the dog warden (Worcestershire Regulatory Services) on 01905 822799, weekdays 9am to 5pm, or use their online form. Stray dogs they collect go to their kennels.
Cats and other pets: ring local vets, check with the microchip databases and put up notices.
Keep your pet's microchip details up to date.

topics.title: Animals are loose on the road
steps: If they're a danger to traffic, call 999. Otherwise call 101, and tell the farmer if you know whose they are.
Don't try to herd them yourself.

topics.title: You find fly-tipping
steps: Don't touch it: it may be dangerous, and it may be evidence.
Report it to Wychavon District Council through GOV.UK's fly-tipping page.
If you see someone dumping rubbish, note the time, place and vehicle registration, but only if it's safe.

topics.title: A tree is down, or there's a pothole
steps: If a fallen tree is blocking a road dangerously, call 999. If it's on a power line, keep well away and call 105.
Otherwise report fallen trees, potholes, broken streetlights and blocked drains to the county council online or on 01905 765765.

topics.title: A footpath is blocked
steps: Report it to Worcestershire County Council's rights of way team using their online form. Give the footpath number if you can (it's on the waymarker or the map).
See also our Walks & footpaths page.
